note: Fits well on four criteria and fails the fifth largely because it was never tested. He clears the money test despite refusing to pay — 'I have that money saved' — which makes this a willingness loss, not an affordability one, and exactly the distinction the stated ICP conflates. He is unambiguously good-to-great and not deconditioned: three years of unbroken training, zero to 12 pull-ups, benching around bodyweight, 74 kg at 175 cm, plateaued and wanting the next level. Health is the neglected corner — a multi-year back complaint he has never had looked at. The 'successful' criterion is recorded as a miss because nothing in the call establishes it: the rep never asked what he does, and the only occupational signal is a rotating shift rota including overnight cover, which points to employment rather than ownership. That gap is itself the finding — the rep ran a full hour without ever learning the prospect's occupation, then guessed wrong about why he was hesitating on price.
